solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Person who formulated law for King Edward, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the man behind ... law, that anything that can go wrong will
second meaning: King Edward is a potato variety

explanation.walkthrough: King Edward looks like a monarch, but it is a British potato variety; murphy is an old Irish-flavoured slang word for any potato.
explanation.definitionFit: The adage 'whatever can go wrong will' bears the surname, and the same name is informal slang for a spud.

clue.text: Some cream is sour in this state

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: In one particular place, part of the cream has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state in the Midwest, whose largest city is Kansas City, is the place being pointed at.

clue.text: Shoots messengers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: plant stems that grow along the ground and root
second meaning: ... carry messages on foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots messengers' reads as a grim act, but the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Strawberry plants send out runners as new growth, and couriers who carry dispatches were called runners.

clue.text: Notice good person in centre providing first aid for competitor

indicators.note: in means the notice and the good person go inside the word for centre

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre
an ad is a notice in a paper
ST, saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: A medic treats a competitor near the middle of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first aid' looks medical, but means a help given at the very start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage granted at the start of a race is literally the first help a competitor gets.

clue.text: Leave the field, having secured a point

parts.note: having something means being with it
in football a draw secures one point

explanation.surface: A player or team goes off the pitch once a point is safely in the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull out of a contest or retreat from the battlefield is to quit the field.

clue.text: Undistinguished duo that made first appearance together

definitions.text: Undistinguished duo that made first appearance together

parts.words: Undistinguished duo that made first appearance together
parts.note: undistinguished means impossible to tell apart, and the pair were born at the same time, a joint debut

explanation.walkthrough: 'Undistinguished' looks like an insult, meaning mediocre; here it means they cannot be told apart, and the first appearance is birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Siblings from a single fertilised egg look alike and are born on the same occasion.

clue.text: Poet animated head of American family

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ancient Greek poet of the Iliad and the Odyssey
second meaning: ... Simpson, father in the cartoon The Simpsons

explanation.walkthrough: One name serves both the Greek epic poet and the cartoon dad.
explanation.definitionFit: The epic bard and the father in The Simpsons share this first name.

clue.text: Voiced private bitterness

indicators.note: voiced means the word is spoken out loud and what is heard matters

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, such as a private

explanation.surface: A personal sense of resentment is finally expressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like an adjective, secret, but it is a soldier, a ranker; said aloud that sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated resentment or ill will, a lingering bitterness.

clue.text: Friendliness increasing worldwide, supposedly

definitions.meaning: second meaning: under global warming, heat is said to be rising across the planet

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a wry nod to global warming; 'supposedly' hedges the climate claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial affection is described as warmth, and warmth is also physical heat.

clue.text: In troubled state, courage that'll stop one getting cold feet

definitions.text: that'll stop one getting cold feet

parts.note: to be in hot water is to be in trouble
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble shows the courage not to lose their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold feet' suggests losing nerve, but means literal chilly feet in bed; bottle is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber bag filled with hot water is put in bed to keep the feet warm.

clue.text: Musically perform comic opera in Eastern state

parts.note: to perform musically with the voice is to sing

indicators.note: comic here means the letters of opera are played about with, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer is invited to stage a comic opera somewhere in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic opera' reads as a genre, but 'comic' scrambles OPERA into APORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The island city-state at the tip of the Malay peninsula is a sovereign country in the East.

clue.text: Finishes off mine, ore being insignificant

indicators.note: finishes off means each of the two following words loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Mining operations wind down because the ore left is not worth much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishes off' applies to both words: MINE loses its last letter to give MIN, and ORE loses its last letter to give OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something minor is of small importance or trivial, just as an insignificant matter is.

clue.text: Kept an eye on some bowling leading to a wicket

indicators.note: leading to means the first piece comes in front of what follows

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so some bowling is several overs
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket spectator watched a spell of bowling that ended with a wicket falling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six deliveries; W stands for a wicket on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee something is to supervise it, keeping watch over how it goes.

clue.text: Expel from courses in error

parts.note: racecourses are known collectively as the turf
a calculation in error is out, i.e. wrong

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown off racecourses for making a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The turf' is horse racing and its courses; 'out' as in 'your figures are out' means mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrasal verb means to eject or throw somebody out of a place.

clue.text: One emperor turned back follower of another

indicators.note: turned back means the pieces are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: one is a, as in a single thing
a tsar was a Russian emperor

explanation.surface: One ruler turns away and becomes a disciple of a rival monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'another' is a second emperor: Rastafarians revere Haile Selassie, Emperor of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian venerates Haile Selassie, so is a devotee of a different emperor from the one in the clue.

clue.text: Strange act one follows with another, having little to say

indicators.note: follows means one comes after the rearranged letters
strange signals that the letters of act are made odd, rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
another go is a turn, as in 'have another'

explanation.surface: An odd performance is followed by a second one, and the performer stays quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is not a second act but another go, a turn, as in 'whose turn is it?'.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person is reserved and uncommunicative, saying very little.

clue.text: Meeting in open competition in Paris?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a private conversation between two people
second meaning: the French literally means head-to-head, a direct contest

explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means head-to-head; in Paris marks the foreign phrase, with the question mark flagging the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A private conversation between two people is called by this French phrase, literally head to head.

clue.text: Okay, or better than okay

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an expression of agreement, all right
second meaning: extremely well, more than just fine

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is grudging agreement and also high praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a reply it signals assent; taken literally it means in an excellent manner.

clue.text: History exam relating to country

parts.note: history is the past
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A history test on the subject of the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life and the countryside, often with sheep and shepherds.

clue.text: Liberal hugged by a devotee everywhere

indicators.note: hugged by means the liberal's letter is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: a lover is a devotee, as in a music lover

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is embraced by a fan wherever they go.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means across the whole area, in every place.

clue.text: Liking sculptor's first piece in gallery

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

indicators.note: first piece means the opening letter of sculptor's

explanation.surface: An admirer is fond of a sculptor's first work on show in a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of British national art galleries, the best-known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste for something is a fondness or preference for it.

clue.text: Stays if reforms meet required standard

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are formed again in a different order

explanation.surface: An institution stays in business provided its changes reach the expected level.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy a requirement is to fulfil or comply with it.

clue.text: Mixed drink, for example, before decoration's put up

indicators.note: before means the example abbreviation comes ahead of the next piece
put up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: decoration's is decoration is; a gong is slang for a medal or honour

explanation.surface: A cocktail is made, for instance, before the Christmas decorations go up.
explanation.walkthrough: Gong is British slang for a medal; read upwards in this down clue it gives GNOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a blended drink of eggs, milk, sugar and often spirits, served at Christmas.

clue.text: Scientist showing a lot of effrontery to one pope

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: gall is cheek or effrontery
one is the Roman numeral I
Leo is the name of thirteen popes

explanation.surface: A scientist shows great cheek towards a pope, as famously happened with the Inquisition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims GALL to GAL; the surface nods to the real astronomer's clash with the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian astronomer and physicist championed the Copernican view of the solar system.

clue.text: Stout or light beer's moved right into the middle

indicators.note: moved means a letter shifts position within the beer
into the middle says where the shifted letter ends up, at the centre

parts.note: lager is a light beer; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A drinker debates stout versus lager, the right choice shifting to the middle ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the dark beer, which fits the lager theme, but it means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A stout person is big or heavy-built, so large describes them.

clue.text: Revision of the law ultimately costly for rich

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the letters of the law are rearranged
ultimately means the final letter of costly

explanation.surface: Changing the law in the end proves expensive, so only the rich benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revision of' rearranges THE LAW into WEALTH; 'ultimately' gives Y from costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wealthy means having plenty of money, a synonym for being rich.

clue.text: Emphatic refusal from Guinevere

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the inside of the name

explanation.surface: Guinevere firmly turns down an advance, perhaps from Lancelot or Arthur.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinevere was King Arthur's queen in the legends.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'not ever' is a strong, unequivocal way of saying no.

clue.text: State most points at least twice after short time

indicators.note: after means the compass letters come behind the time abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
three of the four compass points, east, north and south, each appear at least twice: E, N, N, E, S, S, E, E

explanation.surface: Someone announces that most points were scored at least twice after a brief spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The points are compass points: E, N and S (most of the four, W missing) each turn up two or more times.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a US state in the South, home of Nashville and Memphis.

clue.text: Person responsible for plots exploded grenade in front of king

indicators.note: in front of means the rearranged letters precede the king's letter
an exploded grenade is blown apart, so its letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A conspirator responsible for plots sets off a grenade before the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plots' suggests conspiracy against the king; here they are garden plots.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends beds and patches of land in a garden looks after plots.

clue.text: Doctor in strange case set about 27's neighbour

indicators.note: about means the word for set goes around the neighbouring state's code

parts.note: to jell is to set, as a jelly does
Kentucky borders Tennessee (27 across); KY is its postal abbreviation

explanation.surface: A doctor in a puzzling medical case sets out to visit a nearby state.
explanation.walkthrough: Stevenson's novella is 'Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde', so 'strange case' is a title, not a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The respectable physician who becomes Mr Hyde is the doctor of Stevenson's Strange Case.
